text.p: Lithuanian newspapers carried the following reports in their Thursday editions. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- Parliament approved state guarantees for foreign loans of up to 101.5 million litas for construction of the Butinge Nafta oil terminal. The sum is expected to cover half the construction costs.

- The state security department is investigating a version of the Miami nuclear weapons scandal that suggests that the affair was the work of Russian special services in an effort to hurt Lithuania's aspirations to join NATO.
- Kaunas brewer Ragutis said it made 2.3 million litas profit during the first half of 1997 compared to 1.5 million litas in the first half of 1996.

- Klaipeda brewer Shvyturys led the market in beer production in the month of May, brewing 2.92 million liters of beer. According to preliminary figures, Shvyturys brewed 3.1 million liters in June. No comparative figures were given.
- Litimpeks Bank said that following the completion of its 60 million litas share emission, foreign capital controls 76 percent of the the bank's shares.
- A SAS MD-81 returned to Vilnius international Airport, unable to complete its flight to Copenhagen due to technical problems on Wednesday. The MD-81 was in the air for 15 minutes.

- The price of the new $200 million eurobond will be decided on July 10. The government hopes to sign an agreement with Western banks on July 15. It will be the biggest issue of government securities and its five-year maturity the longest.

- According to a Respublika/Baltijos Tyrimai poll, one-third of voters surveyed said they would vote for Lithuanian-American Valdas Adamkus, a former environment protection agency official, as president.

- Polish and Lithuanian parliamentarians gathered in their first joint assembly in Vilnius on Wednesday. Lithuanian President Algirdas Brazauskas urged the group to deal with the Warsaw-to-Helsinki highway project, the Via Baltica.
